newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P assigns BBB l-term rating to Banca Pop Brescia.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BBB l-term rating to Banca Pop Brescia.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said it had assigned triple-B long term and A-3 short term counterparty ratings to Banca Popolare di Brescia scrl (Bipop) and the outlook on the ratings was negative.

An S&P statement received in Milan said the ratings were based on the bank's strong track record, sophisticated management "relative to that of peers", its innovative approach to products and their delivery.

"These positive factors are offset however by the financial effects and managerial challenges presented by Bipop's recent ambitious acquisition of 50 northern Italian branches from the troubled Banco di Napoli and the effects this has on the combined entity's asset quality, capital and funding profile," it said.

S&P said the acquisition of the Napoli branches increased the overall asset base by one-fifth and although it would potentially improve the bank's market position, its large size was considered inherently risky.
"Additionally, the emphasis of the acquired branches differs markedly from Bipop's target clients, which are small and medium size companies and entrepreneurs."
It said the acquisition caused "significant stress" to the bank's financial profile and S&P had some concerns about deterioration in asset quality for the whole group.

Napoli branches had weak deposit bases and it would be necessary for Banca Popolare di Brescia to fund a large part of the acquired loan book from the interbank market short term until it could increase deposit bases.

"Capital resources will be depleted with the overall risk adjusted solvency ratio expected to fall below the eight percent minimum at year-end 1996 although the more important Tier-1 ratio will remain above the four percent minimum."
But it expected regulatory capital levels to be restored by the year end and through the acquisition it gained access to a well spread network with good potential for its credit and savings products.
"The negative outlook expresses Standard and Poor's concerns regarding the manageability of the acquisition in the increasingly competitive banking environment in Italy," it said.

"It also indicates the reduction in the bank's financial flexibility, at least in the short term," it said adding further expansion via acquisition was out of the question until the bank's position had stabilised.
"Barring evidence of such stabilisation, the group's ratings will confront downward pressure," it said.
